title: Speculative decoding on our AWQ targets
subtitle: 2x RTX 3090 (24GB), TP=2. Qwen3.8-27B DSpark: SGLang v0.5.22, measured 2026-10-31 on the SHIPPED config (SPEC_DECODE=1: fp8_e4m3 KV, true 262144 window, bf16 draft) — natural-text prompts, cache flushed per point, same-day plain-arm A/B at the 10-31 levels (custom allreduce, INT8 lm_head). EAGLE3 / DFlash rows: v0.5.12, 2026-05-29, BF16 drafts.
footnote: DSpark rows (2026-10-31): natural-text prompts (Open-Platypus haystack), greedy, fresh prefill (/flush_cache per point), 100-tok outputs, same-boot plain-arm A/B — bench_long_context.py --prompt-source natural; random prompts are NOT a spec-arm instrument (degenerate continuation, near-perfect draft: 230 tok/s at 262K). The short-context ratio is task-dependent (a passage summary is a predictable continuation; the 2026-09-27 code-prompt receipt read 1.6×). Live bake-off traffic (temp 1.0, opencode): accept length median 3.10 over the first 3,199 decode batches. FP8 bars: not on this lane - the FP8 W8A8 MoE kernel does not compile on Ampere sm_86 (Triton rejects e4m3) and single-user decode is weight-byte-bound, so AWQ int4 wins even where FP8 is native (R9700: Coder-30B AWQ 56 vs FP8 38 tok/s). Receipts: benchmarks/qwen38/natural-vs-random-2026-10-31/, benchmarks/fp8-vs-awq-coder-reap.json.
